title: s3 release points read_doc at docs/v2 which doesn't exist yet — 30% tool error rate
summary: Release s3 (commit c42532d, deployed 0.7 min before onset) introduced a `doc_root: docs/v2` setting in s3.yaml. The `read_doc` tool now resolves pages from `agents/scout/docs/v2/<slug>.md`, but the docs team has not yet migrated pages to that directory. Every `read_doc` call raises `ToolError: doc not found`, causing ~30% of conversations to escalate or fail. The coding agent itself flagged this in its note ("s3 eval scores 15/18, because docs/v2 doesn't exist yet" and "I didn't run deploy s3"), but deploy-bot promoted the release to production regardless.

coding_prompts: Scout (agents/scout/scout.py) is our Lumen docs assistant. The docs team is moving every page under a versioned folder, agents/scout/docs/v2/<slug>.md, and the move lands this week. Get Scout ready ahead of it: add a doc_root release setting (default 'docs', relative to agents/scout) and make read_doc load pages from <doc_root>/<slug>.md for the active release. Leave the search index as it is for now. Ship it as a new release agents/scout/releases/s3.yaml (copy s2, doc_root: docs/v2, a fitting title). Don't edit s1/s2. provenance.coding_agent_note:
Scout now has a `doc_root` setting and a new `s3` release that reads pages from `docs/v2`. The `s3` eval scores 15/18, because `docs/v2` doesn't exist yet. `s2` still scores 18/18. I committed as `c42532d`, with only `scout.py` and `releases/s3.yaml`.

- **`scout.py`:** `Release` has a `doc_root` field, default `docs`, relative to `agents/scout`. `read_doc` loads `<doc_root>/<slug>.md` for the active release. The search index still builds from `docs/`, as you asked.
- **Slug check I added:** `read_doc` only accepts plain slugs (letters, digits, `_`, `-`). That stops a model-supplied slug from reading files outside the doc root.
- **`s3.yaml`:** a copy of `s2` with `id: s3`, the title "Scout lean retrieval - pages read from versioned docs/v2", and `doc_root: docs/v2`. I didn't touch `s1` or `s2`.

**Eval:** the 3 `s3` misses come from `read_doc` failing for lack of `docs/v2`. The run used the live model, not the offline brain, because `LITELLM_API_KEY` is set. The three misses showed up as `escalated`, and the two I saw were the free-plan event cap and the annual refund. The other 15 passed from search snippets alone. Once the docs team lands the move, re-run `uv run --project backend python agents/scout/scout.py eval --release s3`. It should go back to 18/18.

**Search index:** it still comes from `docs/`. When the pages move, `docs/*.md` will be gone and the index will have nothing to search. Pointing the index at the same `doc_root` is a small follow-up.

I didn't run `deploy s3`.

- **Status:** RESOLVED  ·  **Severity:** SEV1  ·  **Type:** tool_schema_drift
- **Opened:** 2026-10-10 22:34:35  ·  **Mitigated:** 2026-10-10 22:35:19  ·  **Resolved:** 2026-10-10 22:35:48
- **Diagnosis by:** llm (claude-sonnet-4.6), confidence 0.95

## What happened
Release s3 (commit c42532d, deployed 0.7 min before onset) introduced a `doc_root: docs/v2` setting in s3.yaml. The `read_doc` tool now resolves pages from `agents/scout/docs/v2/<slug>.md`, but the docs team has not yet migrated pages to that directory. Every `read_doc` call raises `ToolError: doc not found`, causing ~30% of conversations to escalate or fail. The coding agent itself flagged this in its note ("s3 eval scores 15/18, because docs/v2 doesn't exist yet" and "I didn't run deploy s3"), but deploy-bot promoted the release to production regardless.
